prompt: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art sprite concept for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up: a single GYRE enemy of the Iron Tide, a spinning ring-gun drone from a steel fortress, isolated. A thick circular gunmetal ring like a heavy riveted wheel rim, with a bright steel highlight along its top-left arc and dark iron shading on the bottom-right, studded with a circle of small glowing amber rivets. Inside the ring, four straight steel spokes cross to a round central hub with a dark armored cap and a small hot amber core light. Exactly four short stubby gun muzzles stick straight out from the outer rim at the top, bottom, left and right, each a squared barrel with a dark bore and a brass collar, making the silhouette a ringed cross. Open gaps between the spokes. Symmetric, mechanical, readable silhouette. Front view, flat and face-on, centered with a generous empty margin on all sides on a perfectly flat solid pure bright green chroma-key background that fills the whole image and shows through the gaps. Crisp chunky pixel art with a 1-pixel near-black navy outline at the sprite's native pixel scale, flat saturated fills with three-step shading ramps lit from the top-left, bold simple shapes that stay readable at small size, no anti-aliasing, no motion blur, no scenery, no stars, no cast shadow, no glow bleeding onto the background, no text, no labels.
